A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a distributed NUCA L2 cache with a dynamic cache management mechanism that maps data to cache slices and cache bins dynamically is an attractive alternative to the conventional shared cache design in a many-core processor to obtain high performance for both single-threaded and multi-threaded workloads.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the conventional single-threaded shared L2 cache design may not be the best choice for future many-core processors.
, in order to achieve high program performance, the future many-core processor must provide a distributed cache architecture and a dynamic cache management mechanism.

, by considering both cache access latency and miss rate when mapping data to distributed NUCA L2 caches, we can significantly improve the single thread program performance on future many core processors.
